name: CMER-Bench
description: Mathematical Expression Recognition (MER) has made significant progress in recognizing simple expressions, but the robust recognition of complex mathematical expressions with many tokens and multiple lines remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we first introduce CMER-Bench, a carefully constructed benchmark that categorizes expressions into three difficulty levels: easy, moderate, and complex. Leveraging CMER-Bench, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of existing MER models and general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The results reveal that while current methods perform well on easy and moderate expressions, their performance degrades significantly when handling complex mathematical expressions, mainly because existing public training datasets are primarily composed of simple samples. reputation: A specialized benchmark for mathematical expression recognition that targets complex multi-line expressions and is relevant to the MER research community.
notes: Focuses on harder expressions than typical MER datasets; likely small relative to large-scale pretraining corpora and may expose strong distribution shift from common training data.
